name: Vedic study (vedādhyayana / svādhyāya)
method_summary: Learning one's own Vedic recension by recitation from a teacher, as enjoined by 'one's own Veda is to be studied'; in the Mīmāṃsā account it precedes, and makes possible, the inquiry into the meaning of Vedic sentences.
prerequisites: initiation into Vedic study (upanayana), per Dharmaśāstra

name: Inquiry into dharma (dharma-jijñāsā, vedārtha-vicāra)
method_summary: Systematic investigation of the Vedic sentences by the adhikaraṇa method — subject, doubt, connection, prima facie view, conclusion — undertaken after Vedic study, before the student returns home, to know dharma for performance.
prerequisites: completed study of one's Vedic recension

name: Sacrifice (yāga) as analysed in Mīmāṃsā
method_summary: The principal enjoined act: offering a substance with reference to a deity named in the injunction or mantra, with its subsidiaries in fixed sequence; it produces the apūrva that yields the fruit.

name: Agnihotra (the daily fire offering)
method_summary: The obligatory morning and evening offering in the sacred fires, enjoined for life; Mīmāṃsā uses it as the example of an originative injunction ('he offers the Agnihotra') and of a name known from another text (MS 1.4.4).
notes: Procedure belongs to the śrauta manuals (U01/U02); only its Mīmāṃsā treatment is recorded here.

name: New- and full-moon offerings (darśapūrṇamāsa)
method_summary: The archetypal iṣṭi (prakṛti), all of whose subsidiaries (e.g. the prayājas) are taught in its own context, from which ectypal offerings take their procedure; enjoined for one desiring heaven.

name: Jyotiṣṭoma (the model soma sacrifice)
method_summary: The archetypal soma rite ('one desiring heaven should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma'), whose basic form is the Agniṣṭoma; Śabara names it as the paradigm of what leads to the highest good.

name: Setting up the sacred fires (agnyādhāna / agnyādheya)
method_summary: The rite establishing the householder's sacred fires, prerequisite to śrauta rites; its text names the three higher varṇas, which Ātreya uses to restrict eligibility (MS 6.1.26).

name: Viśvajit (the rite of giving away all)
method_summary: A rite in which the sacrificer gives away all he owns; no fruit is stated, so heaven is understood (MS 4.3.15); what one is master of is given, but not the land, which is common to all (MS 6.7.1–3).

name: Śyena (a sorcery rite)
method_summary: A rite the Veda states as the means for one who wishes to harm an enemy. Mīmāṃsā records it only to show that the Veda does not enjoin harming: the rite is described as a means, not as a duty.

warnings.text: The Śyena and similar rites (Vajra, Iṣu) are harmful (anartha): their aim is violence, violence is prohibited, and they lead to sin (pratyavāya); they are not dharma.

name: The Agnīṣomīya animal offering
method_summary: The model animal rite of the soma sacrifice; in Mīmāṃsā the reference point for the question whether killing enjoined within a rite is sin (see dsp:sacrificial-killing).

warnings.text: The general prohibition 'one should not harm any being' stands; Mīmāṃsā and its critics (Sāṃkhya, Jains, Buddhists) disagree whether a ritual injunction exempts the act from sin.

notes: Summary only; no procedure recorded. Low confidence on the Mīmāṃsā references beyond the general debate.

name: Expiation (prāyaścitta)
method_summary: Occasional rites enjoined on the occasion of a fault, omission or mishap in performance (treated in MS 6.4 and elsewhere).

name: Performing obligatory and occasional rites while abstaining from desire-prompted and prohibited acts
method_summary: The discipline of the one seeking release: continue the obligatory and occasional rites to avoid the demerit of omission (and, for Kumārila, to destroy past sin), abstain from desire-prompted acts that would produce new bodies and from prohibited acts; past karma is exhausted by experience.
prerequisites: eligibility for Vedic rites; aversion to saṃsāra (Śāstradīpikā, Prakaraṇapañcikā)

name: Self-knowledge supported by calm, restraint and celibacy (Prābhākara)
method_summary: Knowing the self as distinct from body, senses and cognition, cultivated together with calm (śama), restraint (dama), celibacy and the like; enjoined for non-return, it destroys the store of karma (Prakaraṇapañcikā). For Kumārila, self-knowledge removes the desire through which fruits accrue.

name: Performing dharma as an offering to the Lord (īśvarārpaṇa)
method_summary: Doing the enjoined acts with the thought of offering them to Śrī Govinda (Āpadeva) or Īśvara (Laugākṣi Bhāskara), which makes dharma a cause of the highest good; the Gītā's 'whatever you do, do it as an offering to me' is cited as authority.
